facts.invariant: Advertised operations are a typed operation-id set with grant, task-mode, and redaction disposition; generic_api_request never counts as coverage.
Each semantic invocation has one call id, operation id, input digest/redaction disposition, and exactly one typed result receipt.
A denied operation yields a typed safe receipt naming the failed boundary; secret values and hidden identifiers are absent.
A mutation receipt carries operation id, idempotency key, outcome, stable code, retryability, and safe current revision when applicable.
Every artifact ref is produced by a typed semantic receipt or registered control-plane work product, and is linked to the terminal result by run id.
Interaction and approval targets are immutable revision/decision references carried in a typed target envelope, not an unconstrained request payload.
A blocked or yielded result names a bounded owner/action or continuation kind; wake routing remains a control-plane decision and emits only safe causal identifiers.
A budget/cost stop includes a typed stop reason, observed limit class, safe usage aggregate, and control-plane decision id.
Source-event idempotency is already replay-safe; semantic mutation idempotency additionally requires a stable operation receipt/audit ref.
The controller binds behavior to the negotiated typed booleans/version and treats unsupported required versions as fail-closed.
Run, session, turn, item, source-event, work-assessment, status-decision, request, and receipt identifiers form an acyclic trace from command to terminal decision.

Checkout/release, wake routing, budget enforcement, audit persistence, run persistence/replay, assignment, and monitor management are not runner tool calls and must not be serialized as semantic operations.

Cross-company discovery, broad audit access, destructive document lifecycle, and company administration require separately governed product contracts; v1 must reject rather than tunnel them through generic payloads.
Every accepted additive correction ships a golden replay, duplicate/retry, redaction/denial, and unknown-version fixture before it is called direct support.
